turns.user: Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter disruption?

answer.answer:
Of the 7 Midwest hubs, Minneapolis is the most exposed to winter disruption by a wide margin, with a winter sub-score of 75.9 — driven by 34.6 observed winter-disruption days per year (snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C), the highest observed count in the portfolio (rank 1) — plus FEMA NRI components WNTW 47.7 and ISTM 32.0.

Detroit is second at 43.5: only 10.4 observed disruption days/yr (portfolio rank 5), but much higher FEMA NRI winter inputs (long-term score 63.8; WNTW 77.1, ISTM 50.4). Chicago is third at 35.9 (11.8 days/yr, portfolio rank 4; NRI long-term 38.6). The remaining four cluster closely: Kansas City 30.5 (8.2 days/yr), Indianapolis 27.7 (7.0), St. Louis 26.7 (5.2) and Columbus 26.3 (6.2 days/yr, tied on observed days with Newark).

For resilience investment, Minneapolis is the clear winter priority; Detroit and Chicago are secondary. Note that winter is only a top composite driver for Minneapolis, Detroit and Chicago — the other Midwest hubs are driven more by severe storm and flood.

Minneapolis leads on both observed frequency (34.6 days/yr, portfolio rank 1) and overall winter score (75.9).
Detroit ranks 2nd on winter score despite fewer observed days, because its FEMA NRI winter inputs are much higher (WNTW 77.1, ISTM 50.4).
Noted that scores blend observed disruption-day frequency with FEMA NRI percentiles, and that Columbus ties Newark on observed days.

Observed days use the stated rule (snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C) at a point location near each hub.

turns.user: Why is the top one there so exposed?

answer.answer:
Worth flagging the premise: Memphis isn't very exposed to winter in absolute terms — it just tops a low-scoring group. Its winter sub-score is 18.0 and its overall composite is 27.0, which is tier "Low" (rank 13 of 22 hubs).

What gives Memphis the highest Southern winter score is mostly the FEMA NRI side, not observed weather. Winter blends observed frequency (weight 0.6) with the NRI long-term score (weight 0.4). Observed: just 2.0 winter-disruption days/yr (snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C) over 2021-2025, which normalizes to only 5.8 and ranks 14th in the portfolio. Long-term: NRI score 36.3, the mean of WNTW 31.5 and ISTM 41.1 — i.e. meaningful ice-storm loss exposure. Supporting evidence: 2 Winter Storm and 2 Severe Ice Storm federal major-disaster declarations since 2000.

Winter contributes only 4.5 points to the 27.0 composite. Memphis's actual top drivers are flood (score 51.8, contributing 10.4 — 2.4 heavy-rain days/yr at >= 50 mm, portfolio rank 5 tied with Los Angeles; NRI IFLD 40.3) and severe storm (score 38.3, contributing 7.7 — NRI TRND 87.7, SWND 29.1, HAIL 3.8; 14 Severe Storm declarations since 2000). If you're spending in Memphis, flood and tornado/severe-wind resilience is the better target; winter spend would be about rare ice events.
